annotations.text:
The signed-in product: prove it works.

Build your agent → call it yourself with real borrower context → see exactly what it captured. Everything here is real data from real test calls; there is no dialling yet, so there is no Runs screen and no invented pipeline numbers.

Read the top row left to right — that is the journey.

1 · FIRST RUN
The most important screen in the product, and usually the worst one anywhere.

The band carries the next step instead of a statistic. The three steps are numbered because this genuinely is a sequence — not decoration.

2 · TODAY, WITH DATA
The old ops funnel (queued → dialled → connected) is gone: without dialling it would be theatre.

What replaced it is how your agent is actually doing — promises captured, right-person rate, what still needs a human.

3 · CONVERSATIONS
The dense one. Every row carries the borrower's own sentence as a second line — a call centre gives you a disposition code, this gives you what they said.

Vermilion appears only where a person has to act.

4 · DETAIL — THE CENTREPIECE
Every captured field points back at the line that produced it: the promise date says "from अठारह तारीख को सैलरी आएगी", and that line is marked in the transcript.

This is the trust mechanism. A collections head has to believe the extraction before they will act on it.

5 · SCRIPT EDITOR
Shown as the conversation it produces, not as a form. Labels are plain questions — "Opens with", "Who it is" — never "System Prompt".

The right rail states the compliance rules that are NOT the user's to edit, rather than hiding them. Test is one click, in place.

6 · TEST A CALL
Borrower context is the change here: loan, amount, due date. The agent can then say the real figure instead of something vague — and these are exactly the fields a borrower list will carry later, so none of it is throwaway.

Reachable from a script, from Today, and from the header.
